solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Irish lake Mike crossed by shallow vessel's tiller

indicators.note: the vessel is crossed, cut through, by the lake and Mike, so they go inside it

parts.note: a pan is a shallow cooking vessel
lough is the Irish word for a lake
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A curious description of a boat crossing an Irish lake, with somebody steering it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiller' suggests a boat's steering bar, but here it means someone who tills the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tills fields with a plough is a farm labourer, literally a tiller of the soil.

clue.text: Legendary prince's abilities, missing the crossbar

indicators.note: a capital letter T without its horizontal bar is left as a single upright stroke, which looks like I

parts.note: parts are talents or abilities, as in 'a man of many parts'

explanation.surface: A mythical prince whose talents fall short, as if he failed to clear a crossbar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing the crossbar' turns the T of PARTS into I: take the bar off a T and an upright I remains.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Trojan prince who abducted Helen bore this name, sparking the Trojan War.

clue.text: Never working, good-for-nothing

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a person of no account is worthless, a good-for-nothing

explanation.surface: A scornful verdict on an idle layabout who has never done a day's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic way of saying not under any circumstances, a synonym for never.

clue.text: Upcoming fashion, say, including a thousand anoraks?

indicators.note: the reversed pieces take the thousand inside them
in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: mode is a fashion or style
e.g., 'for example', is signalled by say
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: Talk of a coming fashion trend that features a great many anoraks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' reverses the fashion and 'say' together in this down clue, and 'including' takes the thousand inside. 'anoraks' is British slang for obsessive enthusiasts; the question mark flags the not-a-coat sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoraks are obsessive hobbyists, so collectively they form the world of nerdy enthusiasts.

clue.text: Fake illness needs mother to stay around

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
to linger is to stay around, reluctant to leave

explanation.surface: A child pretends to be sick so that mother will stay close by.
explanation.definitionFit: To shirk work by pretending to be ill is precisely what feigning sickness amounts to.

clue.text: Crazy career representing teachers' interests?

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
a job is one's occupation or career

explanation.surface: A daft-sounding job description: a career spent looking after teachers' interests.
explanation.walkthrough: A union job, working for the NUT (the former National Union of Teachers in Britain), is literally a career representing teachers' interests.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, a crazy is an informal word for a deranged person, a slang equivalent.

clue.text: Wrap up tool making small holes in wrap

parts.note: wrap up is slang for be quiet, which sh demands
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing small holes

explanation.surface: Instructions to pack away a tool used to punch small holes in fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up' is the British slang command to stop talking, here SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment draped around the shoulders is a wrap, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Slur lacking in gossip for ruler's wife

indicators.note: the slur is lacking the word in, so those letters drop out

parts.note: an insult is a slur
ana is a collection of anecdotes or gossip about someone

explanation.surface: A rumour-mongering slur against a monarch's consort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in' takes IN from INSULT, leaving SULT. 'ana' is a crossword favourite for a set of anecdotes.
explanation.definitionFit: The consort of a sultan carries the feminine title, so she is the wife of a Muslim ruler.

clue.text: Prone or flat in compact form?

definitions.meaning: prone means inclined or liable to do something
The short form of apartment, which is a flat

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a person lying flat might be squeezed into a smaller shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Being likely or inclined to do something is being prone to it; and apartments are abbreviated this way in listings.

clue.text: We initial changes to prepare an ambush

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone swaps around the initials on a document to lay a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal oneself and wait for a victim is to set up an ambush, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Not the leader in tangerine-coloured product line

indicators.note: the word for the colour loses its leading letter

parts.note: tangerine is a shade of orange

explanation.surface: A new range of goods coloured like tangerines, minus its flagship.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's set of related products is called its line or its selection of goods.

clue.text: Last piggy in toilet let out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the preceding words are put out of order

explanation.surface: A pig being let out of a toilet, the final one of the litter.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'This little piggy' counts a child's toes, ending on the smallest.
explanation.definitionFit: In the toe-counting nursery rhyme the final piggy is the smallest digit of the foot.

clue.text: Good reception on a TV I fixed, first having substitute set off

parts.note: a stand-in is a substitute
to go is to set off

indicators.note: fixed suggests the letters are repaired into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fixing a TV for good reception, after first putting a replacement in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good reception' looks like a TV signal; it is an audience's response. 'first having' places STAND-IN and GO ahead of the rearranged ONATVI (VATION).
explanation.definitionFit: An audience rising to applaud gives a performer a warm welcome, the warmest reception there is.

clue.text: Careless, having DIs leave blame

indicators.note: the detectives leave the word, so their letters drop out

parts.note: indiscriminate means done without care or judgement
DIs are detective inspectors in the British police

explanation.surface: Careless detectives depart, with the blame left behind for others.
explanation.definitionFit: To accuse someone of a crime is to lay the blame on them.

clue.text: Letter replaces later one read aloud at opening of vegetable hamper

indicators.note: the first letter named takes the place of the second at the start of the vegetable

parts.note: a cucumber is a salad vegetable
Q, a letter later in the alphabet than N, is spoken as cue
en is the spelt-out name of the letter N

explanation.surface: Swapping letters around at the start of a vegetable hamper, as if packing a Christmas box.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening CU of CUCUMBER, which sounds like the letter Q, is replaced by EN, the name of N, which comes earlier in the alphabet. 'hamper' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper is to hinder or burden, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Sod's green after treatment is absorbed

indicators.note: the letters are treated, worked into a different order

explanation.surface: A lawn's turf, once treated, soaks up the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sod' is a piece of turf here, though it reads as a rude word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deeply absorbed in a task is wholly engaged by it, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Authoritarian, no saint, before a panel

indicators.note: no says the saint is taken away from the authoritarian

parts.note: a fascist is an authoritarian

explanation.surface: A dictator, no saint, appears before a panel of judges.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia is a flat board, such as a dashboard or a shop's nameboard, which is a kind of panel.

clue.text: Trick with passion round back of bottling plant

indicators.note: the trick and passion together go round the letter taken from bottling

parts.note: to fox is to trick or baffle
love is passion

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A crafty ploy combined with an enthusiasm for bottling homemade preserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis, the tall flower with bell-shaped blooms, is a garden plant of this name.

clue.text: Surly politician tucked into more than half of Swiss cheese

indicators.note: the politician is tucked inside the cheese
four of the seven letters of the cheese are kept, more than half

parts.note: Gruyère is a Swiss cheese
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered politician tucks into a generous portion of Swiss cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than half of' keeps four of the cheese's seven letters, GRUY, with the politician tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Surly and bad-tempered are synonyms, both describing an irritable mood.

clue.text: Baked dish with no cover on top is unevenly coloured

parts.note: a pie is a baked dish
bald means with no hair covering the head

explanation.surface: A pie baked without a lid comes out patchily browned.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with irregular patches of black and white is piebald, so the coat is unevenly coloured.

clue.text: Banks maybe partly backing Yeltsin at oblast

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Financial institutions half-supporting Boris Yeltsin at a Russian regional district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' is not the plural of bank: it is Sir Joseph Banks, the naturalist on Cook's voyage. An oblast is a Russian province.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Banks was a famous plant scientist, so he is an example of the profession, as 'maybe' signals.

clue.text: 7 nabbing Spanish boy's fruit

indicators.note: the answer to 7 nabs, grabs hold of, the boy's name inside it

parts.note: the answer to 7 down, a word for prone or a short flat
Rico is a Spanish boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone snatching a Spanish lad's fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange-yellow stone fruit is related to the peach and plum.

clue.text: Difficult driving plane when one's out of it?

indicators.note: one is taken out of the word for driving a plane on the ground

parts.note: an aircraft taxiing moves along the ground under its own power
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Is it hard to steer an aircraft along a runway when you're not quite all there?
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of it' suggests being dazed, but it says I leaves TAXIING.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxing task is demanding, requiring effort, so it is hard or difficult.

clue.text: Threatened with crumbled Stilton coating, the man would rage

indicators.note: the crumbled cheese goes around the other pieces like a coating
crumbled says the cheese's letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: he'd is short for he would
anger is rage

explanation.surface: A man is threatened with a crumbled cheese coating and would fly into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbled' rearranges STILTON (a British blue cheese) into ONT and LIST, which coat HED ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being listed as at risk, like a critically ill patient or endangered species, means being threatened.

clue.text: Lush plant in new container looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to repot a plant is to move it into a new pot

explanation.surface: A luxuriant plant moved into a new pot, now perking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like an adjective for green growth; it is a noun, a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is slang for a heavy drinker, and a toper is an old word for a habitual drunkard.

clue.text: Hugging brat (a jerk) is extremely pleasant

indicators.note: the word for extremely hugs the other pieces, which go inside it

parts.note: so means extremely, as in 'so kind'
an imp is a mischievous child, a brat
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: Cuddling a spoilt brat, even a jerk, is very nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico, borrowed from Italian and Spanish, means likeable and congenial, so pleasant.

clue.text: Finalists in ballroom drama cut a rug

indicators.note: the finalists are the final letters of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Finalists in a dance competition, after drama, cut a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut a rug' is slang for dancing, but here 'cut' gives its last letter and 'rug' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small floor covering, such as a doormat or rug, is a mat.

clue.text: Grip bit of seafood softly

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish, an item of seafood
p is piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Holding a piece of seafood gently.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a tool that holds things tightly, and to clamp is to grip firmly.

clue.text: Was "courting" old-fashioned?

definitions.meaning: courting is going out with someone romantically, having seen them socially
out of date or no longer in style

explanation.surface: Was the word 'courting' itself a quaint, outmoded term?
explanation.definitionFit: Going out with someone is seeing them romantically, and old-fashioned things belong to a past era.

clue.text: Spooner's optimal equipment for offer at pub?

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, signals a sound swap

parts.note: best is optimal
gear is equipment

explanation.surface: The ideal kit to offer customers at a pub, as Spooner might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of BEST GEAR. A British pub's guest beer is an ale from another brewery, offered for a limited time.
explanation.definitionFit: A visiting ale stocked for a short while is something a pub offers its drinkers.
